title: kv-cache: adaptive eviction + spillover memory manager to reduce fragmentation and paging
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: KV cache fragmentation and frequent paging/spillover under sustained multi-tenant workloads cause increased tail latency and higher GPU memory churn. This PR implements an adaptive eviction and spillover memory manager plus defragmentation hints to reduce paging, improve median/tail latency, and lower overall token cost. Summary of changes: 1) Add a new spillover allocator (runtime/kv/spillover_manager) that tracks page utilization and coalesces adjacent free ranges before spilling to host memory. 2) Implement adaptive eviction priority that combines recency, token frequency, and allocation fragment size to prefer evicting small fragmented entries first. 3) Introduce a lightweight background defragmentation pass that runs opportunistically during low-util periods and exposes a tunable budget. 4) Add kernel-level flags to the serving runtime so the allocator can request contiguous pages when available; fall back remains unchanged. 5) New metrics and traces for fragmentation_ratio, spillover_rate, avg_eviction_cost, and defrag_time. Design notes: The spillover manager operates as a cooperative component with the existing KV cache: it does not synchronously block hot-path lookups and uses epoch-based reclamation to avoid race conditions with GPU threads. Eviction scores are normalized per-model to avoid cross-model bias. The defragmentation pass performs in-place compaction where possible, but will prefer copy-and-free only if contiguous blocks can be reallocated without exceeding the budget. Rollout plan: feature gated and rolled out via canary to 5% of serving clusters for 48h, monitor fragmentation_ratio and spillover_rate, then ramp to 25%/24h and 100% if stable. Benchmarks: see perf section below. Backwards compatibility: no API changes; config defaults preserved. Related: ENG-3421 implements the monitoring dashboard and alerting thresholds, SUP-2148 surfaced customer-observed paging during incident INT-978. Testing: unit tests for allocator invariants, integration tests simulating multi-tenant eviction pressure, and perf harness runs across a mix of short/long seq workloads. See changed files for small illustrative patches and test vectors.
commit_summary: a1c9f33: feat(kv): add spillover manager with coalescing allocator and eviction hooks
b7d2e8a: perf(kv): adaptive eviction priority using recency+freq+fragment_size
c3f4b91: infra: expose defrag budget and tuning knobs via runtime config
d5e8f44: tests(kv): add eviction/defrag integration tests and harness scenarios
e8a1c77: docs: kv-cache memory management overview and rollout notes
review_comments: Carlos Gutierrez: Could the adaptive eviction score overweight tiny fragments and cause cache churn on hot sequences? Please show perf numbers broken out by short/long sequence workloads.

Aisha Raman: Good catch. The eviction score includes a per-model normalization and a hot-sequence penalty. Added microbenchmarks for 8/64/512 token sequences in the perf section. Results show negligible churn on 8-token workloads and 18% median latency reduction for mixed workloads.
Mei Li: I noticed the defrag pass can be CPU-heavy in worst case. Can we bound its budget tighter and expose a knob? Also add safety to avoid running while heavy GC is active.
Aisha Raman: Added defrag_budget_ms and defrag_cpu_limit config knobs and a safeguard to pause defrag while major GC/compaction cycles are running. Reduced default budget to 25ms every 10s in canary.
Tomás Ortega: CI integration tests flaked once on the snapshot race — please ensure epoch-based reclamation prevents races between GPU readers and defrag compaction.
Aisha Raman: Implemented an epoch barrier and additional unit tests that assert no stale pointer use during defrag; added a CI-only stress test to the integration matrix.
ci_checks: Integration tests: initially failed (snapshot-race), fixed and passing
Benchmarks: perf-run/kv_mixed_sequence: improved median latency 18% and 95p latency 12% reduction on canary hardware
Stress test: pass (1000 concurrent sessions simulated)
bench_results: spillover_rate: reduced from 14.2% -> 4.7% under 90th percentile load
fragmentation_ratio: reduced from 0.37 -> 0.12 after defrag pass over 30m
perf_notes: Observed the best improvements on mixed workloads with long-lived contexts that previously caused fragmented allocations. Short, very hot single-shot workloads show neutral change. Memory overhead of defrag metadata is ~1.2% of KV footprint and configurable.
release_notes: Improve KV cache memory management: adaptive eviction policy, coalescing spillover allocator, and opportunistic defragmentation. Expected to reduce paging and tail latency for multi-tenant workloads. Rollout is feature-gated; monitor fragmentation_ratio and spillover_rate.
notes: Feature gated behind kv_cache.adaptive_eviction=true. Observability dashboards added under 'KV Cache / Memory'. Canary started 2025-11-15 and promoted after stability checks.
qa_steps: Enable feature gate on a canary cluster and run kv_bench workload (8/64/512 tokens) for 2 hours
Verify fragmentation_ratio < 0.2 and spillover_rate < 6% during steady-state
Confirm no increase in error rates and validate epoch barrier unit tests
Ramp to 25% traffic and repeat checks before full rollout
